problem: Existing embodied navigation tasks assume well-defined instructions, and prior interactive benchmarks are small, room-level, or only let the oracle describe the target instance. There is no large-scale dialog-augmented training data or online oracle evaluation for house-scale, long-horizon instance navigation.
motivation: Real-world instructions are often vague, e.g. only the object category, so agents must ask questions to resolve ambiguity and to guide exploration. Studying this needs both training data with dialogs and an automatic oracle that can answer attribute, route and disambiguation queries.
key_idea: Define Interactive Instance Goal Navigation (IIGN) and build VL-LN Bench: an automatically generated set of ~41k dialog-augmented house-scale trajectories plus a GPT-4o/rule-based oracle for online evaluation, used to train a Qwen2.5-VL agent that navigates and asks questions.
insight: Dialog reduces exploration failures (IIGN 89→71, IGN 84→46) and ambiguity failures (IGN 143→124, IIGN 159→145). The main bottleneck is image–attribute alignment, with about 73% of failures being detection errors. Agents ask less informative questions than humans (Human-Human 93% SR with ~2 turns versus VLLN-D 16–17%). The turn-limit ablation shows the biggest gain from 1 to 2 turns, because one turn is usually spent on an attribute question.
method: IIGN task: the agent gets a category-only instruction and acts with FORWARD 0.25m, TURN 30°, LOOK-UP/DOWN, ASK, STOP; success means stopping within 0.25m of any viewpoint of the target instance.

Oracle: GPT-4o plus rules; it classifies each query as attribute, route or disambiguation. Attribute answers come from instance metadata. Route answers convert the first 4m of the shortest path, simplified to waypoints and anchored to salient objects, into language. Disambiguation answers 'yes' if the target is centered in view and within 3m.
Scene metadata: MMScan room-level annotations merged into house-level instance and region dictionaries, plus an Sr3D spatial-relation graph (edges within 1m) for discriminative descriptions.

Episode generation: start poses from R2R-CE (72 scenes) and 18 self-annotated scenes; a partial instruction (category only) and a GPT-4o full description per instance; viewpoints from the 3D bbox expanded by 0.6m.

Trajectory collection: a frontier-based explorer with a GT detector picks the frontier nearest the previous one with 90% probability and the frontier nearest the target with 10%; it asks an attribute question at the start, a route question on choosing the best frontier, and a disambiguation question when a same-category object is seen; templated questions are logged with sensor data.

Agent training: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct trained with the InternVLA-N1 recipe on VLN data plus ObjectNav (23,774), IGN (11,661 filtered) and IIGN dialog data; the variants VLLN-O, -I, -D differ in data mixture.
MSP metric: mean gain in success rate over the no-dialog baseline across dialog budgets 1..n (n=5), measuring both dialog usefulness and efficiency.

setting.training_data: InternVLA-N1 VLN data + 23,774 ObjectNav trajectories + 11,661 filtered IGN trajectories (VLLN-I no dialog, VLLN-D with dialog); the VL-LN dataset has 41,891 IIGN dialog trajectories with 95,559 dialogs, and 5,087 IGN trajectories were collected in total
setting.action_space: low-level: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN ±30°, LOOK-UP/DOWN, ASK, STOP
setting.privileged: Oracle has full environment knowledge (target attributes, location, shortest path); GT detector and GT semantics only for data collection, not for the evaluated agents

numbers.extra: trained with dialog data; oracle answers via GPT-4o; up to 5 dialog turns
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Results of the VL-LN Benchmarks, IIGN VLLN-D row

numbers_note: Benchmarks are the paper's own (VL-LN); the test split is 500 episodes. The text also cites VLLN-O at 59.3% SR on ObjectNav without a table. Cross-role results are on a 100-episode subset.
results: VLLN-D reaches SR 20.2 on IIGN and 25.0 on IGN, beating the no-dialog VLLN-I (14.2 / 22.4), VLFM (10.2 / 12.6) and FBE (8.4 / 7.4). Human-Human reaches 93% SR, so a large gap to agents remains.
limitations: Absolute success stays low (20–25%), and image–attribute alignment is a bottleneck (73% of failures are detection errors).
The oracle is GPT-4o with rules and asks more turns of human users than a human oracle would; the training dialogs come from scripted templates, so the agent's questioning is limited to ~1–2 turns.
Scale is limited to MP3D (90 scenes), simulation only; the agent needs 3,200+ GPU-hours to train.
